prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1438; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a side impact at a signalized intersection. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Witness statements and the report both support that the claimant was present.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene show some details of the impact, though no independent witnesses to the collision have come forward. The damage pattern is mostly consistent with the described side impact.

Entry 4: Claimant's medical records describe a shoulder injury that is plausible for a crash of this type. No prior injury to the same area is known from the records available so far.

Entry 5: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Requested additional treatment notes to understand the course of care.

Entry 6: Claimant gave a follow-up statement with some additional small details about the collision. The core account has stayed the same across both statements.

Entry 7: Checked vehicle history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 8: Confirmed the driver lives with the policyholder and qualifies as a covered household member. Claim remains open pending review of the treatment records.
